newsitem.title: IRAQ: Rapturous welcome for Uday by Iraqi media.
newsitem.headline: Rapturous welcome for Uday by Iraqi media.

text.p: Iraq's official media gave a rapturous welcome on Wednesday to President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday after he appeared on television in a hospital bed five days after being wounded in an assassination attempt.
State-run newspapers ran articles, poems and commentaries on how glad the Iraqis were to see Uday.

Uday appeared on television on Tuesday evening for the first time since he was shot as he drove through Baghdad's wealthy al-Mansour district on December 12. He seemed to blame Iran for the attack but did not mention Iraq's neighbour by name.

Uday spoke at ease with a Qatari envoy and a reporter from the official Iraqi News Agency. He looked relaxed with his body covered by a blanket and no bandages on his head, but he did not move either hand to welcome the visitors.
Uday, 32, is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee. He owns the newspaper Babel, Iraq's most influential, and runs the popular Shebab television channel.
Pictures of Uday speaking to the Qatari envoy were splashed on the front pages of the ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra and the official al-Iraq.
The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya devoted its back page to the television images which put to rest rumours that Saddam's son was in a serious condition.
Festivities were said to have continued throughout the night and one newspaper reported that celebrations were held across the country immediately after Uday was seen.
"For the fifth day, thanksgiving prayers, sacrifices and folk parties continue in Iraq," declared Jumhouriya.
State-run television and radio interrupted programmes to receive congratulations from well-wishers. Shebab television broadcasts scenes of revellers dancing in Baghdad to folk music.
Uday was variously described as "Iraq's lion cub" and "the beauty of youth".
Uday's newspaper Babel published a poem congratulating Saddam on the safety of his son: "Saddam! You are the sword of Iraq. You have won your cub. Safe remain your eyes."

Uday was quoted by official media as describing the attack as "treachery" and said it was not a characteristic of Arabs. He implicated Iran, saying: "The treacherous people are known along with the place they come from....they tested us for eight years" -- a reference to the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
Iraqi opposition groups abroad have claimed they were behind the attack.
"What I feel now from this condition is the same felt by a military commander dear to me being subjected to the same situation," Uday said without elaboration.
The spot where Uday was shot has turned into something like a shrine, frequented by thousands of Iraqis, slaughtering sheep and handing out sweets.

Shopkeepers in al-Mansour district where Uday was attacked have raised banners wishing Uday a speedy recovery. Several restaurants offer free meals and butchers in the area are said to have been handing out meat free of charge.
